title: God gives Job boldness as a prize
english: By the principle of creation, then, we have been separated from all the animals. But if you are a sinner, a fornicator, bent toward earth, you have not been separated from the four-footed creatures of the earth. You have been compared to the beasts, and you have become like a horse and a mule, which have no understanding, and like a horse in heat.

Chapter 40. “No, but gird up your loins like a man” (Job 40:7). The full prizes of the contests are stored up for those who have fought well after this life, but even now the grace of God gives an earnest to the athletes. So when Job fought his greatest contests—when he lost his possessions and glorified the One who gave them; when he laid aside his children and gave thanks to the One who took them; when he fell ill so that worms rained from his body and was not conquered by his pains—God gave him preludes and an earnest of the prizes by addressing him through cloud and whirlwind.

After hearing the earlier words, then, when he ought to answer God, he is silent, as though he did not have boldness. For he did not yet know the saying, “Moses spoke, and God answered him with a voice” (Exodus 19:19). But God gives him boldness to speak, and so great is His kindness that He takes on the role not of a judge but of one being judged alongside the human being. Other Scriptures taught this too, such as, “Come, and let us reason together” (Isaiah 1:18), and, “My people, what have I done to you?” (Micah 6:3).

God is already giving him a prize, because He questions a human being, because He inquires of him, because He gives him authority to answer. If he had not conquered, he would not have received it. If he had not endured, he would not have heard, “Gird up your loins like a man” (Job 40:7), and do not be silent, but act like a man in the face of the questions. For as long as someone's loins are not girded and bound tight but are slack, he cannot answer God with good reason.

Let no one, then, answer God before he has become a man perfect in spiritual stature and has girded his loins. “Do not reject my judgment” (Job 40:8). Do not suppose that what you endured has been judged by me without reason, and do not reject my judgment.

orientation: Origen is expounding God's address to Job in Job 40, explaining that God's command to gird the loins is a gift of boldness given to Job as a proven victor.
